item.title: Who is Stephen Miller, the new gateway man to Trump – podcast
item.description:
Jonathan Yerushalmy and Reged Ahmad examine the Democrats failed impeachment attempt against US defence secretary Pete Hegseth and ask – could we see another bid soon?

The other Donald Trump appointee making headlines is the president’s new chief-of-staff, Stephen Miller. Known as the architect of Trump’s tough immigration policies, the appointment is seen as a clear sign Trump has no intention of playing nice with the other side, despite indicating he would do just that after the Republicans massive midterms loss. Jonathan looks back at Miller’s past to try and decipher how a descendent of a family fleeing persecution developed such hardline views that he has been condemned as a white nationalist

item.title: Trump could be about to sell out Ukraine. Europe must get its act together, fast | Paul Taylor
item.description:
A deal giving Moscow a slice of Ukrainian territory and sanctions relief could be on the table in weeks – yet European leaders are busy squabbling

Donald Trump has lost substantial power over domestic policy after last week’s devastating midterm losses, but his ability to cement his legacy by upending US foreign policy remains largely intact.

There is every reason to fear a ”great betrayal” of Ukraine in the coming weeks, one that would reward Vladimir Putin for Russia’s war of aggression against Kyiv, and also do lasting damage to the European security order. Yet lilliputian European leaders are too busy squabbling over who should represent them in future peace talks to focus on how to prevent a sellout. Despite fundamental European interests being at stake in this week’s three-way US-Russia-Ukraine negotiations in Abu Dhabi, Europe is relegated to a side room, represented by a posse of officials from the UK, France, Germany, the EU and Nato.

item.title: Nima Momeni sentenced to 16 years to life in murder of Cash App founder Bob Lee
item.description:
Tech consultant convicted of second-degree murder in 2023 stabbing death of Cash App founder

Nima Momeni, the man convicted of murdering Cash App founder Bob Lee, has been sentenced to 16 years to life.

Momeni, 42, has been in San Francisco’s county jail since late April of 2023, after he was arrested in connection with the stabbing death of Lee, who had created the mobile payment service and was serving as the chief product officer of the cryptocurrency MobileCoin at the time of his death.
